references.text: Egyptian magicians used their secret arts to imitate Moses' signs, just as they do here with the frogs.
The magicians in Egypt did the same with their secret arts when water was turned into blood, a pattern repeated with the plague of frogs.
The magicians could not produce gnats and acknowledged that this was God's finger—a contrast to their ability to imitate the frog plague.
The magicians could not stand before Moses because of the plague of boils, which shows their limitations compared to God's power.
Jannes and Jambres are mentioned as those who opposed Moses, traditionally identified as the Egyptian magicians who imitated God's signs.
Unclean spirits that looked like frogs came out of the dragon's mouth—an apocalyptic parallel to the plague of frogs in Egypt.

The verses highlight the connection between the magicians' limited ability to imitate God's signs (succeeding with frogs, failing with gnats) as a theological point about their ultimate powerlessness.
